result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers are single paragraphs of roughly 90 words with no lists, preamble or closing offer, and both correctly contrast observing a few people to learn why with measuring many users on a metric to learn which version wins. A adds the useful point that A/B testing needs traffic, while B notes that usability tests work on rough prototypes and ends with a memorable framing. Neither invents statistics, so the two are effectively equal. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers are single paragraphs of about 90 words with no lists, preamble or closing offer. Each correctly contrasts a usability test, which watches a few people to learn why things go wrong, with an A/B test, which compares two versions on a metric across many live users to see which wins. A adds that usability tests work on rough prototypes and B adds that A/B tests need traffic, so neither is clearly stronger.
